children: Hour Loop, Inc.

HOUR shares have lost 21.5% in the past three months against the industry’s 1.3% growth. It has also lagged the broader Zacks Retail-Wholesale sector’s 3.9% decline and the S&P 500’s 0.1% increase in the same time frame. Hour Loop faces challenges from heavy Amazon dependence, rising fulfillment costs, margin pressure, tighter liquidity, working-capital needs and inventory management risks.
What’s Weighing on HOUR’s Performance?

Hour Loop’s heavy reliance on Amazon remains a key business risk. Approximately 97% of revenues in the first half of 2026 were generated through or with Amazon, while Walmart and Hourloop.com remain negligible contributors. This concentration exposes the company to changes in Amazon’s fees, fulfillment rules, disbursement policies and Buy Box dynamics. Any unfavorable platform change, service disruption or loss of competitiveness could pressure sales, margins and cash generation and heighten earnings volatility.

Margin pressure remains another headwind despite strong top-line growth. The company operates in a hypercompetitive e-commerce environment, where pricing must balance sales volume with profitability. Amazon’s revised FBA fee structure and a 3.5% fuel and logistics surcharge have added operating costs, while selling and marketing expenses continue to rise with revenues. In the second quarter, operating income and net income declined year over year even as revenues increased sharply, limiting operating leverage.

Liquidity has tightened as growth absorbs more working capital. Cash declined to $1 million as of June 30, 2026, from $3.8 million as of Dec. 31, 2025, while operating cash outflow increased to $3.6 million in the first half of 2026. Higher inventory purchases and delayed Amazon remittances drove much of the cash use. The company also received $1.6 million of related-party advances, while repayment obligations on affiliated loans could place additional pressure on available cash during periods of rapid expansion.

Inventory management presents another headwind, given Hour Loop’s broad assortment of more than 100,000 SKUs. Slow-moving products can require promotional discounts or inventory write-downs, which may pressure margins if demand shifts unexpectedly. The company records a full allowance for SKUs not sold for more than one year, while its strategy of maintaining product availability requires substantial inventory investment. This creates exposure to obsolescence, weaker-than-expected demand and higher carrying costs.

Changes in Amazon’s operating requirements are also increasing fulfillment complexity. Amazon discontinued labeling and packaging services for sellers in 2026, forcing Hour Loop to use external fulfillment partners or integrate compliant labeling and packaging at the manufacturing source. These steps increase variable fulfillment, cost-of-revenue, and selling expenses. Although vendor discounts and advertising support have helped offset the impact, labeling-related costs are expected to continue going forward.
Stock Valuation

The stock is currently trading at a discount compared with the historical levels and industry average. It is trading at a trailing 12-month EV/sales multiple of 0.39X compared with the industry’s figure of 2.11X. It is also lower than two of the company’s peers,
Groupon, Inc.
GRPN and
Pattern Group Inc.
PTRN, which stood at 1.02X and 1.08X, respectively.
Can HOUR Power Through the Challenges?

Hour Loop is benefiting from sustained top-line momentum as its e-commerce model continues to mature. For the first six months of 2026, revenues advanced 20.7%, with order volume up 15%. U.S. and international revenues also increased, while stronger customer activity and continued operating-model development provide a favorable base for further growth. The company also remained profitable through the period.

The company’s technology-enabled platform is another key tailwind. Its proprietary software processes large volumes of data to identify product gaps, optimize inventory and support year-round availability, while automated repricing tools help balance competitiveness with margins. Hour Loop also plans to expand business managers, vendors and SKUs. Greater advertising support and better vendor discounts have helped offset rising costs and support profitability, strengthening the platform for expansion.
Wrapping Up

Despite Amazon concentration, margin pressures and tighter liquidity, Hour Loop’s revenue momentum, technology-driven platform and vendor support provide meaningful growth potential. Also, the stock seems undervalued at the moment. Therefore, the decline in its share price presents a lucrative opportunity for investors to add the stock to their portfolio.
